A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same DF3DV-1K dataset, benchmark and DI2FIX enhancer. v1 ends after its references despite citing supplementary items; v2 includes Sections S.1–S.4. Their reported content can be compared reliably, without assuming what unseen earlier supplementary material contained.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten radiance-field methods in Table 3 and DI2FIX enhancement and ablation results in Tables 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and supplies detailed supplementary results, paired significance tests and a view-dependent-static-object evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions describe the same DIFIX adaptation using rendered reference views and LPIPS-filtered training pairs. Section S.3 newly discloses disabling the Gram-matrix loss, but presents this as a detail of the existing adaptation; it does not establish a procedural revision from v1.

E1.justification: Both use RobustNeRF, On-the-go, DF3DV-1K and DF3DV-41, retaining the same 1,048 scenes and 17 challenging scenarios. The added masked-region diagnostic selects existing DF3DV-41 scenes. Changes to the dataset catalogues in Tables 1–2 do not change evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains 3DGS and the same nine distractor-free methods, including both T-3DGS variants. The enhancer comparison retains Vanilla, DIFIX, DIFIX+RobustNeRF and DI2FIX. Supplementary comparisons use these existing methods without introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Section S.2 adds a diagnostic evaluation using three images from each of 18 DF3DV-41 scenes, with human-annotated masks targeting view-dependent static regions. Preprocessing, configuration and cross-method training details disclosed elsewhere in the supplement do not establish changes to the existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 supplies detailed scenario analyses, the complete cross-method ablation matrix and extensive qualitative and failure examples, substantially expanding inspectable evidence for analyses summarized or cited in v1. It also adds the distinct investigation of distractor removal versus preservation of view-dependent static objects in Table S.5 and Figure S.7.

E5.justification: v2 introduces paired t-tests across scenes for the top four methods on PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS, with p-values in Table S.1; v1 reports no corresponding statistical analysis. This adds substantial inferential reporting, without documenting increased runs or seeds. Table S.7 mentions error bars but supplies no uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 3–6 remain unchanged. v2 adds substantial scenario-level, per-method enhancement and cross-method result entries. The new masked-region study reports, for example, 23.19 dB PSNR for AsymGS versus 21.35 dB for 3DGS in Table S.5; these are additional diagnostic results, not performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive theoretical propositions, proofs or derivations. The LPIPS filtering condition is retained, and the supplement adds no new formal mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three contributions: the large dataset, systematic ten-method benchmark and DI2FIX enhancement application. The claimed average improvements remain 0.96 dB PSNR and 0.057 LPIPS; additional supporting evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that distractor-removal benefits generally outweigh damage to view-dependent static appearance, and explains the complementary roles of natural long-tail data and the curated subset. Existing severe-corruption and confirmation-bias limitations receive fuller mechanism explanations. Its broad interpretation of ranking significance needs qualification given the large p-values for some pairs.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset and leaderboard access information, licensing, directory structure and annotation guidance. It also discloses 8× downsampling, configuration and instability-handling policies, and DI2FIX loss settings, batch size 1, two L40 GPUs and approximately 3–4 days of training. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing reruns.

R1.justification: Six references are added, including OpenCV, Gram-matrix style-transfer, view-selection and clustering work. Tables 1–2 revise dataset descriptions and classify RealX3D and D-RE10K-iPhone as public. The central positioning around large-scale casual-capture benchmarking remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact, with localized wording, caption and cross-reference edits. v2 updates author contribution markings, adds acknowledgements and organizes supplementary explanations into Sections S.1–S.4. The added scientific material does not entail extensive rewriting of the main argument.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual presentation through Tables S.1–S.7 and Figures S.1–S.19, including significance displays, scenario matrices, comparison galleries, failure examples and distribution charts. Some panels repeat existing main-text examples. Tables 1–2 are also reorganized, while the main experimental displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v1 repeatedly cites supplementary evidence and experimental details absent from its PDF. v2 supplies that material, adds practical access and implementation information, and makes robustness and generalization claims substantially easier to assess. The static-region diagnostic and statistical comparisons provide useful additional scrutiny. Some significance wording overreaches the evidence, such as the RobustSplat–DeGauss SSIM comparison with p=0.82, but this limited weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in completeness and reproducibility.
